weakest_scene.root_cause: A comparison-row template was used for a 100x population explosion. The number lives only in the label, and Data's poses are not attached to anything.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Draw the urchin explosion from urchins: one urchin multiplies into a carpet of about 100 spiny purple urchins covering the seafloor. Data does the multiplying, for example tipping a bucket that pours urchins out. Keep the 10,000% label secondary to the swarm.

A bubble-size comparison, 100% vs 1%, with Data perched on top. It is a chart, not sea stars.
Two labelled rows. The 10.1K% is text only, and nothing urchin-shaped appears.
The same bubble machine as seg1, reused for kelp canopy at 100% vs 4%.

grades.one_line: A strong three-step ecological chain is told with gauges, bubbles and labelled rows: no sea stars, no urchins, no kelp is ever drawn, and Data poses beside charts instead of causing anything.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3 to seg1:start): a static ruler gauge reading '99% apart' with Data shuffling. The hook and seg0 are one recycled picture for about 6s.
seg1 and seg3 use the identical bubble-comparison template, so the video repeats itself.
seg2 is a bare number card: '10.1K%' as text with no urchin swarm.
None of the story's subjects (sea star, urchin, kelp) is ever drawn. Kelp appears as land-tree icons in seg4.
Data is decorative throughout (perching, pointing, cheering) and celebrates on the 100% pan during a loss payoff.
The outro text is crowded: the CTA caption, 'COMMENT BELOW' and the sources line are stacked on top of each other. The source line in seg1 is truncated.
fixes: Hook: open on a sea star dissolving or wasting away, with 99 of 100 stars vanishing from a reef in the first second.
seg2: Data pours urchins from a bucket and the seafloor fills with a purple urchin carpet scaled to 100x.
seg3: urchins chew down kelp stalks until 4 of 100 remain. Use a bespoke kelp forest, not a reused bubble chart.
Draw kelp as kelp (tall swaying fronds with floats), not trees. Data's reaction at the payoff should match the loss.
Give the outro caption, the CTA and the sources line their own vertical bands. Shorten the source line so it is not truncated.
